analysis.note: The compound is construed by Śaṅkara as Arjuna’s specifically kṣatriya duty, namely battle.

verification.detail: compound stem svadharma as Pum/Dvitiya/Eka: pass; relation karmadharaya: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: ‘Even/also,’ with scope over svadharmam, as Śaṅkara repeats tam api avekṣya.
Negates arhasi with the infinitive vikampitum: ‘you ought not to waver.’
Infinitive in -tum: ‘to waver/tremble’; Śaṅkara glosses it as pracalitum.
With infinitive, ‘be entitled/ought’; with na, ‘you ought not.’
Adjectival ablative singular agreeing with yuddhāt; sandhi gives dharmyād dhi.
Ablative of comparison with śreyaḥ anyat: ‘than a righteous battle.’
Nominative neuter singular, predicative/subject with anyat and na vidyate: ‘another better thing/good.’
Negates vidyate: ‘is not found/does not exist.’

justifications.decision: Translate svadharmam not as an abstract ‘personal religion’ but as Arjuna’s own class-duty: for a kṣatriya, battle. The accusative is the object of avekṣya, ‘having regard to/considering.’
justifications.chosen: svadharma = the kṣatriya’s own duty, namely battle

evidence.quote: svadharmam api svo dharmaḥ kṣatriyasya yuddhaṃ tam api avekṣya
evidence.translation: ‘svadharmam api’: one’s own dharma; for a kṣatriya it is battle—considering even that.

justifications.decision: The finite arhasi with the infinitive has normative force; the negation is not a simple prediction but ‘you ought not / it is not proper for you.’ Vikampitum is taken as ‘to waver, be shaken,’ glossed by pracalitum.
justifications.chosen: na vikampitum arhasi = you ought not to waver

evidence.translation: You ought not to waver, to be unsettled.

justifications.decision: The reason svadharma bears on Arjuna is that it is the kṣatriya’s natural/innate dharma. This supports ‘your own duty’ rather than merely a chosen or private obligation.
justifications.chosen: the duty is rooted in kṣatriya nature

evidence.quote: kṣatriyasya svābhāvikād dharmād ātma-svābhāvyād ity abhiprāyaḥ
evidence.translation: The purport is: because of the kṣatriya’s natural dharma, because of his own nature.

justifications.decision: Dharmya qualifies yuddha and is not a mere label for warfare generally: this battle is ‘not departed from dharma’ because it serves dharma and the protection of subjects through conquest of the earth.
options_considered: ‘lawful/just war’ in the sense explained by the commentary
justifications.chosen: dharmya yuddha = righteous battle, not any battle as such

evidence.quote: tac ca yuddhaṃ pṛthivī-jaya-dvāreṇa dharmārthaṃ prajā-rakṣaṇārthaṃ ceti dharmād anapetaṃ paraṃ dharmyam
evidence.translation: And that battle, through the conquest of the earth, is for the sake of dharma and for the protection of subjects; thus it has not fallen away from dharma and is supremely righteous.

justifications.decision: The second half means ‘no other better good exists for a kṣatriya than righteous battle.’ The paired ablatives dharmyāt yuddhāt supply the comparison governed by śreyaḥ/anyat, and kṣatriyasya is the genitive of the person for whom this is so.
options_considered: ‘from righteous battle no other welfare arises’
‘other than righteous battle there is no higher good for a kṣatriya’
‘because there is no battle better than a kṣatriya’
justifications.chosen: dharmyād yuddhāt is the ablative standard of comparison for śreyaḥ anyat

evidence.quote: tasmād dharmyād yuddhāc chreyo 'nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate hi yasmāt
evidence.translation: For, than that righteous battle, no other better thing is found for a kṣatriya.

justifications.decision: The particle hi introduces the reason for the preceding injunction not to waver.

translation:
And even considering your own duty (svadharma), you ought not to waver;
for, for a kṣatriya, no other better good is found than a righteous battle.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render svadharma as vague ‘personal duty’; Śaṅkara identifies it as the kṣatriya’s battle-duty grounded in his nature.
It might make dharmya-yuddha mean ‘religious war’ or any war; Śaṅkara restricts it to a battle not apart from dharma, aimed at dharma and protection of subjects.
It might translate na vikampitum arhasi as ‘you cannot tremble’; the bhāṣya gives the normative sense ‘you ought not to waver.’
It might miss that hi is causal and that dharmyāt yuddhāt is the ablative standard for ‘no other better good.’
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 segmented sva-dharmam as sva + dharmam; I analyze the printed hyphenated expression as the compound svadharmam, following Śaṅkara’s compound gloss ‘svo dharmaḥ ... tam’ (line 1).
ByT5 gives prefixed lemmas avekṣ and vikamp; the required verbal format uses bare roots with prefixes, so these are analyzed as īkṣ with prefix ava and kamp with prefix vi.
In sandhi parsing, cāvekṣya is represented as ca + avekṣya; hence the individual surface_in_sandhi values are cā and vekṣya, preserving the printed sandhi while giving pausal ca and avekṣya.
mula: sva-dharmam api cāvekṣya na vikampitum arhasi | dharmyād dhi yuddhāc chreyo 'nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate
commentary_lines: svadharmam api svo dharmaḥ kṣatriyasya yuddhaṃ tam api avekṣya tvaṃ na vikampituṃ pracalitum nārhasi kṣatriyasya svābhāvikād dharmād ātma-svābhāvyād ity abhiprāyaḥ |
tac ca yuddhaṃ pṛthivī-jaya-dvāreṇa dharmārthaṃ prajā-rakṣaṇārthaṃ ceti dharmād anapetaṃ paraṃ dharmyam |
tasmād dharmyād yuddhāc chreyo 'nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate hi yasmāt ||bhgs_2.31||
kutaś ca tat yuddhaṃ kartavyam iti, ucyate ---
